title: The New-born Child This Early Morn
description: The New-born Child This Early Morn in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Cyriacus Schneegass wrote these words in German. Emanuel Cronenwett's translation was printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 169.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The new born Child this ear-ly morn, The dear Christ child, of vir-gin born, A-gain brings from His heav-enly home A new year to all Chris-ten-dom.

lines: The new-born Child this early morn,
The dear Christ-child, of virgin born,
Again brings from His heavenly home
A new year to all Christendom.
This causes joy to angels fair,
Who love to keep us in their care;
They sing that in this wondrous Child
God now with man is reconciled.
Since God is reconciled with men,
What harm can Satan do us, then?
O’er Satan and the gates of hell
This Christ-child shall for us prevail.
He brings the year of jubilee!
Rejoice! This is a happy day;
The Christ-child drives all care away.

licence: Public domain: Cyriacus Schneegass died in 1597; Emanuel Cronenwett died in 1931.
credits: Words by Cyriacus Schneegass (1546–1597), translated by Emanuel Cronenwett (1841–1931), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
